question: To which family does the 'Touch-me-not' plant belong?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mimosaceae**__

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Touch-me-not** plant, also known as Mimosa pudica*, belongs to the **Mimosaceae** family.
 
• The plant is well-known for its rapid movement, where its leaves fold inward and droop when touched or shaken, a phenomenon called **thigmonasty** or **seismonasty**.
 
• This plant is native to South America and Central America but is now a common invasive weed in tropical regions worldwide.
 
• It is often used in traditional medicine for its various purported health benefits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The family **Mimosaceae** is a part of the order **Fabales** and is closely related to the **Leguminosae** (Fabaceae) family.
 
• Plants in the Mimosaceae family are typically characterized by their compound leaves and small, often fragrant flowers that are usually arranged in spherical clusters.
 
• The **Touch-me-not** plant is often studied in botanical and environmental sciences due to its unique response to physical stimuli.
 
• While primarily considered a weed, it also has ecological value in soil stabilization and as a nitrogen-fixer, benefiting the soil quality in its habitat.
